text:
sre-bot: automated alert: spike in model output anomalies and KV cache reuse errors detected on prod clusters. signature: stale-seq-offsets + cross-request-kv-leak. rolling error rate 12% over 5m :rotating_light:

eric-oncall: I got the page, joining. where's the impact scope? any customers flagged?

ashley-ml: seeing weird tokens leaking between unrelated sessions on two host pools (us-west-2-g4, eu-north-1-a100). repro by simple prompt pair. logs show repeated `kv_fetch(seq_offset=12345) returned entry.owner=request-abc` while request id is different.

kyle-eng: yikes. looks like cache reuse pointer arithmetic bug after the recent continuous-batching change. suspect boundary check on seq offset when evicting/kvcache.wrap-around.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0429-01, severity: sev2, page routed to oncall rotation.

eric-oncall: quick mitigation options: 1) turn off KV cache reuse flag, 2) force single-tenant batches (batch_size=1) for affected deployments, 3) rollback continuous-batching commit. Which is fastest?

ashley-ml: disabling KV cache reuse is lowest-risk and immediate. can flip feature flag via infra-config. batch_size=1 will reduce throughput too much. rollback takes >30m. recommend flip reuse->false then monitor.

kyle-eng: prep commands ready. will start toggle on a small canary then flip cluster-wide if green.

ashley-ml: note: if we disable reuse, KV hit rate will drop and cost per token up, but correctness first.

eric-oncall: go for canary on us-west-2-g4. kyle, run the toggle and post exact command.

kyle-eng: running:
```
# canary toggle
redwoodctl config set kvcache.reuse=false --cluster us-west-2-g4 --env prod --commit-msg "mitigation: disable kvcache reuse due to stale offsets"
redwoodctl rollout watch --cluster us-west-2-g4
```

ops-bot: command executed by kyle-eng at 1895009999.

kyle-eng: canary applied. logs showing immediate drop in `kv_lookup_errors` from 180/min -> 12/min on canary hosts. tailing sample: `ERROR kv_lookup: seq_mismatch request=rq_7734 expected=54321 got=54319` seen before, now gone.

tess-support: heads-up: support queue flagged 3 customers complaining about "weird cross-session completions" in last 40 minutes. names: acme-data, finlytics, safechat inc. marking P1 until we confirm containment.

ashley-ml: running small repro tests against canary, no cross-request leakage now. good sign.

eric-oncall: proceed to flip cluster-wide in waves. keep batch_size unchanged for now. notify customers that we're investigating and mitigation underway.

kyle-eng: rolling config to remaining pools (eu-north-1-a100, ap-south-1-v100) with parallelism=2.

ops-bot: rollout progress: 20% -> 60% -> 100% across targeted pools.

ashley-ml: after global flip, kv_lookup_errors settled to baseline (<5/min), model output anomaly rate back to 0.8% from 12%. tail latency 95p improved by 40ms.

tess-support: updated affected customers with mitigation note: "We detected anomalous token reuse between unrelated requests. We have disabled an optimization (KV cache reuse) while we investigate root cause. No evidence of broad data exfiltration; only a small set of sessions observed. We will follow up with postmortem." customers acknowledged.

eric-oncall: okay containment looks good. need oncall handoff in 45m to kyle for deeper debugging and root cause. I'm going offline after 30m for pager rest.

kyle-eng: I'll take second shift. immediate next steps: reproduce locally with instrumented small batch harness, add seq_offset guards, and add unit test for wrap-around case. planning hotfix: ensure `kv_entry.owner_id` validated against request_id on fetch before reuse.

ashley-ml: also add a short-term safeguard in runtime: on cache hit, validate `seq_offset >= last_served_offset_for_session` and reject if suspicious. will prototype now.

eric-oncall: tagging SRE leads and security to assess sensitive leakage risk. @tess-support keep tracking customer comms.

tess-support: will keep running list. currently 12 sessions across 3 customers impacted, all sampled and scrubbed.

ops-bot: pager handoff scheduled: eric-oncall -> kyle-eng at 1895010800.

kyle-eng: started local repro with continuous-batching enabled; reproducer script below:
```
# repro sketch
for i in 1..1000:
  send(prompt_a) # session A
  send(prompt_b) # session B
  assert outputs not contain tokens from other session
```

ashley-ml: quick note about telemetry: we saw a subtle regression in the batching allocator where `batch.slot_idx` can be reused before `kv_cache` entry `seq_offset` is updated under contention. root cause hypothesis: missing memory barrier in slot-to-kv handoff.

kyle-eng: that matches our instrumentation traces. will add atomic publish on slot pointer and an additional seq check on fetch path. planning safe patch + test, then staged deploy to prod.

eric-oncall: thanks team. logging incident timeline and mitigation steps to INC ticket. will close incident once hotfix is deployed and customer follow-ups are complete.

tess-support: customers request ETA for full fix. propose 48h with regular updates.

kyle-eng: ETA 36-48h for patch, tests, and staged rollout. will aim for 36h.

ashley-ml: follow-up tasks: postmortem, telemetry dashboard for `kv_seq_mismatch`, add canary alert for cross-session token similarity, and add regression test in CI for continuous-batching changes.

eric-oncall: handoff to kyle now. I'm dropping from channel. thanks all. :white_check_mark:

kyle-eng: I have the pager. continuing root cause and fix. closing note: mitigation (kvcache.reuse=false) restored correctness. will update after patch commit and canary tests.

ops-bot: incident update logged to INC-2026-0429-01, status: mitigated, assigned to kyle-eng for RC.
